shots.say: Look at this camel! One hump, two humps!
Why do some camels have one hump, and some have two?
I'm Milo. Let's meet the camels!
Welcome to The Animated Zoo, friends!
Today we meet two kinds of camels!
First, the hot, sandy desert. Hello, Sandy! Hello, Mama!
Look at Mama's back. Let's count her humps.
One! Mama has one hump.
A camel with one hump is called a dromedary.
Say it with me. Dromedary!
Does Sandy's mama have one hump, or two humps?
One! Mama is a dromedary.
Now let's fly far away, to Sandy's camel cousin!
Oh! It is so cold here. This is the Gobi Desert.
And here is Sandy's cousin. Look at her back!
How many humps does she have? One, or two?
Two! One hump, two humps.
A camel with two humps is called a Bactrian camel.
Say it with me. Bactrian!
Look at the letter B. It has two bumps!
B for Bactrian. Two humps, like a B!
Make two humps with your hands. Bump, bump!
One hump, a dromedary. Two humps, a Bactrian!
Which camel has two humps? The dromedary, or the Bactrian?
The Bactrian! Look, the dromedary is taller.
Dromedaries have longer legs.
Bactrian camels are shorter, and heavier.
Stand up tall, like a dromedary. Tall, tall!
One hump, or two? Now you know!
Mama and Sandy live in a hot, dry desert.
The sun is hot. The sand is hot, too!
Fan yourself, like it is hot. Phew!
Is Sandy's desert hot, or cold?
Hot! Dromedaries live in hot, dry deserts.
But Sandy's cousin lives far away, in the Gobi Desert.
It is a rocky desert, in Asia.
There are big mountains, with snow on top.
Say it with me. Gobi!
In winter, it gets very, very cold.
Count the snowflakes with me. One, two, three!
Look! In winter, there is snow!
Can you shiver like Milo? Shiver, shiver!
Is the Gobi cold in winter? Yes, or no?
Yes! Very cold, and snowy.
But in summer, the Gobi gets hot!
Cold in winter. Hot in summer!
Who lives where it snows? The dromedary, or the Bactrian?
The Bactrian! Sandy's cousin, in the snowy Gobi.
Point to the snowflake! Where is the snowflake?
Hot deserts for dromedaries. Snowy winters for Bactrians!
Look at the cousin's coat. It is thick, and shaggy!
Bactrian camels grow a thick coat for winter.
The thick coat keeps her warm in the snow.
Put on a warm, fuzzy coat. Zip it up!
Mama's coat is not shaggy. It is short, and light.
Which coat is warmer in the snow? Short, or thick?
Thick! A thick coat is warm and cozy.
Then spring comes. The snow is gone. It is warm!
Is it winter, or spring? Look at the grass!
Look! Her shaggy coat falls off, in big patches!
Now the patches lie on the ground. Count them. One, two, three!
Plop! Plop! More patches fall off.
Does the thick coat fall off in spring, or stay on?
It falls off! This is called shedding.
Shake, shake! Shake off your winter coat!
Now her coat is not so thick. Just right for summer!
A thick coat in winter. It falls off in spring.
And next winter, a new thick coat grows!
Do you wear a coat in winter?
One hump, or two? Short coat, or shaggy coat!
Time to remember what we learned!
How many humps does a Bactrian camel have? One, or two?
Two! Like the letter B.
Which camel lives where it snows? One hump, or two humps?
Two humps! The Bactrian camel, in the snowy Gobi.
When does the shaggy coat fall off? In winter, or in spring?
In spring! Plop, plop, plop!
Thank you for learning with me, friends. See you at the zoo!
